questions.question: The speed of a car is 36 km/h. How much time (in minutes) will a bus traveling at one-fifth of the speed of the car take to cover a distance of 900 m?
questions.solution:
Speed of the bus = (1/5) × speed of the car

⇒ Speed of the bus = (1/5) × 36 = 36/5 km/h

⇒ Distance = 900 m = 0.9 km

⇒ Time taken by bus = distance/ Speed of the bus = 0.9/(36/5) = 0.5/4 hour

⇒ Time taken by bus = (5/40) × 60 = 15/2 minutes

∴ Time taken by bus is 7(1)/(2) minutes.

questions.question: If X : Y = 13 : 12 and X – Y = 2, then what is value of 2X + 3Y?
questions.solution:
Let the value of X and Y be 13z and 12z

⇒ X – Y = 2

⇒ 13z – 12z = 2

⇒ z = 2

⇒ The value of X = 13z = 26

⇒ The value of Y = 12z = 24

⇒ 2X + 3Y = 52 + 72 = 124

∴ The value of (2X + 3Y) is 124.

questions.question: What is the least number of four digits which is exactly divisible by 2, 4, 6 and 8?
questions.solution:
L.C.M. of 2, 4, 6 and 8 is 24.

⇒ 1000 ÷ 24 = 41.67 (Means 42th term, the least number of four digits)

⇒ 24 × 42 = 1008

∴ The least number of four digits which is exactly divisible by 2, 4, 6 and 8 is 1008.

By option, we can check,

∴ 1008 is divisible by 2, 4, 6 and 8.

questions.question: If the height of an equilateral triangle is 20√2 cm, then what is its area (in cm²)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the equilateral triangle = 20√2

**Formula Used:**

Height of the equilateral triangle = (√{3}/2) × side.

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side².

**Calculation:**

⇒ (√3/2) × side = 20√2

⇒ Side = (40√2)/√3 cm

⇒ Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side² = (√3/4) × [(40√2)/√3]²

⇒ Area of equilateral triangle = 800√3/3 cm²

**∴ The area of an equilateral triangle is 800√3/3 cm².**

questions.question: A train, 700 m long crosses a pole in 35 seconds. How much time does it take to cross a platform of length 740 m?
questions.solution:
Speed = frac{{Distance( {length of train} )}}{{time}}

⇒ Speed = 700/35 = 20 m/sec.

⇒ Time (train takes to cross a platform) = length of train and platform/speed = (700 + 740)/20

⇒ Time (train takes to cross a platform) = 72 seconds = 1 minute 12 seconds

∴ Train takes to cross a platform in 1 minute 12 seconds.

questions.question: The average age of 9 men is 45 years. If the age of one woman is included, then the average age becomes 44 years. What is the age of the woman?
questions.solution:
The average age of 9 men = 45 years

⇒ Total age of 9 men = 45 × 9 = 405 years ---- (1)

⇒ The average age of 9 men and one woman = 44 years

⇒ Total age of 9 men and one woman = 44 × 10 = 440 years ---- (2)

From (1) and (2),

⇒ Age of woman = 440 – 405 = 35 years

∴ The age of the woman is 35 years.

questions.question: Mohit is five times efficient as Rohit. If Mohit can complete the work in 28 days less than Rohit, then in how many days can Rohit alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Let the number of days taken by Rohit be x.

Since efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

⇒ Number of days taken by Mohit = x/5

According to the question,

⇒ x – x/5 = 28

⇒ 4x/5 = 28

⇒ x = 35 days

**Alternate Solution:**

Let the efficiency of Rohit be 1.

⇒ Mohit’s efficiency = 5

Let Rohit can complete the work in x days.

⇒ Mohit’s efficiency × time = Rohit’s efficiency × time

⇒ 5 × (x – 28) = 1 × x

⇒ 4x = 5 × 28

⇒ x = 35

⇒ Total work = Rohit’s efficiency × time = 1 × x = 35

⇒ Rohit alone complete the work = Total work/ Rohit’s efficiency = 35 days

∴ Rohit alone complete the work in 35 days.

questions.question: P sold an article to Q at a profit of 20%. Q sold the same article to R at a loss of 25%. R sold the same article to T at a profit of 50%. If P bought the article at Rs. 100, then at what price did T buy that article?
questions.solution:
The cost price of the article for P = Rs. 100 (given)

⇒ Cost price of article for Q = 100 × 120% = Rs. 120

⇒ Cost price of article for R = 120 × (100 – 25)% = Rs. 90

⇒ Cost price of article for T = 90 × 150% = Rs. 135

∴ T bought that article at Rs. 135.

questions.question: A trader marked up his articles 25% more than the cost price. If he offered a discount of 10%, then what will be his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A trader marked up his articles 25% more than the cost price.

He offered a discount of 10%

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Mark price × (100 – discount)%

Profit% = (selling price - cost price)/cost price × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100.

Mark price = 100 × 125% = 125

Selling price = 125 × 90% = 450/4 = 112.5

Profit% = (12.5/100) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ Trader’s profit percentage is 12.5%.**

questions.question: Average of 50 numbers was calculated as 20 when three numbers 26, 36 and 64 were wrongly read as 31, 46 and 59 respectively. What is the correct average?
questions.solution:
Average of 50 numbers = 20

⇒ Sum of 50 numbers = 50 × 20 = 1000

⇒ Right numbers = 26 + 36 + 64 = 126

⇒ Wrong numbers = 31 + 46 + 59 = 136

⇒ Difference = 126 – 136 = 10

⇒ Now the correct sum of 50 numbers = 1000 – 10 = 990

⇒ Correct average of 50 numbers = 990/50 = 19.8

∴ The correct average is 19.8

questions.question: Rs. 480 is invested at simple interest. It becomes Rs. 520 after 20 months. What is the interest rate per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs 480

Amount = Rs 520

Time = 20 months = 20/12 years

**Concept used:**

{{Simple interest }} = frac{{P times R times T( {in years} )}}{{100}}

**Calculation:**

Simple interest for 20/12 years = Amount - principal = 520 - 480

 

Rightarrow {{}}520 - 480{{}} = frac{{480 times R times 20}}{{100 times 12}}

⇒ 40 = 8R

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The interest rate per annum is 5%.**

questions.question: The monthly incomes of A and B are Rs. 12000 and Rs. 15000 respectively. The monthly expenditure of A is Rs. 8000. If the ratio of the monthly expenditures of A and B is 2 : 3, then what is the sum of their monthly savings?
questions.solution:
Let the monthly expenditures of A be 2x

⇒ 2x = 8000

⇒ The monthly expenditure of B = 3x = Rs. 12000

⇒ The monthly saving of A = monthly income of A – monthly expenditure of A

⇒ The monthly saving of A = 12000 – 8000 = Rs. 4000

⇒ The monthly saving of B = 15000 – 12000 = Rs. 3000

⇒ The sum of their monthly savings = 4000 + 3000 = Rs.7000

∴ The sum of their monthly savings is 7000 rupees.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2400 becomes Rs. 3600 in 6 years at a certain rate of compound interest (compounded annually). What will be the amount after 12 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ 3600 = 2400(1 + r/100)⁶

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁶ = 3/2

For 12 years,

⇒ A = 2400(1 + r/100)¹²

⇒ A = 2400[(1 + r/100)⁶]²

⇒ A = 2400 × (3/2)² = Rs. 5400

∴ The amount after 12 years at the same rate of interest will be Rs. 5400.

**Short trick,**

The amount after 12 years = (3600 × 3600)/2400 = Rs. 5400

questions.question: The ratio of the ages of two persons is 3 : 4. If the age of one of them is greater than the other by 8 years, then what is the sum of their ages?
questions.solution:
Short trick∶

⇒ 4 – 3 = 1 → 8

∴ 4 + 3 = 7 → 8 × 7 = 56 years

**Detailed solution∶ **

Let the age of the first person be 3x.

⇒ The age of the second person = 4x

⇒ The difference in their ages = 4x – 3x

⇒ x = 8

⇒ The sum of their ages = 3x + 4x = 7x = 56 years

∴ The sum of their ages is 56 years.

questions.question: Ravika alone can complete three-fifth of a work in 105 days. Mallika can complete one-third of work in 50 days. In how many days Ravika and Mallika working together, can complete 26/35 of the work?
questions.solution:
Ravika alone can complete 3/5 of a work = 105 days

⇒ Ravika alone can complete the whole work = 105 × 5/3 = 175 days

⇒ Mallika can complete 1/3 of work = 50 days

⇒ Mallika can complete the whole work = 50 × 3 = 150 days

⇒ Together they can complete the whole work = (d₁ × d₂)/ (d₁ + d₂)

⇒ Together they can complete the whole work = 175 × 150/325 days

⇒ Together they can complete 26/35 of the work = {{ }}frac{{175 times 150}}{{325}} times frac{{26}}{{35}} = 60 days

∴ Together they can complete 26/35 of the work in 60 days.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 300 cm². If the length of one of the diagonals of the rhombus is 30 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the second diagonal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The area of rhombus = 300 cm²

The length of one of the diagonals of the rhombus = 30 cm 

**Concept used:**

The area of a rhombus = 1/2 × (diagonal)1 × (diagonal)2

**Calculations:**

The area of a rhombus = 1/2 × (diagonal)₁ × (diagonal)₂

⇒ 300 = 1/2 × 30 × (diagonal)₂

⇒ (Diagonal)₂ = 300/15 = 20 cm

**∴ The length (in cm) of the second diagonal is 20 cm.**

questions.question: If the total number of motorcycles parked is 2300, the number having white colour is how much less than those having the blue colour?
questions.solution:
The number having white colour motorcycle = 18%

⇒ The number having blue colour motorcycle = 21%

⇒ Difference of white and blue colour motorcycle = (21 – 18)% = 3%

⇒ The number having white colour is less than the blue colour motorcycle = 3% × 2300 = 69

∴ The number having white colour is 69 less than those having the blue colour motorcycle.

questions.question: If the total number of motorcycles parked is 2300, then what is the number of red colour motor cycles out of them?
questions.solution:
The number of red colour motorcycles = 12% × the total number of motorcycles

⇒ The number of red colour motorcycles = 12% × 2300 = 276

∴ The number of red colour motorcycles is 276.
